root_cause: The DELETE handler and manager are correct — `remove_from_collection` (collection_manager.rs:159-176) deletes the `LinkedChildren` edge and the unit test at collection_manager.rs:683-690 proves it via the reverse lookup `get_collections_containing_item`. The divergence is in the harness's write-effect read-back, not the write. The effect oracle reads a collection's members back through the forward browse path `GET /Items?parentId={collectionId}`. In Hermit, `GET /Items` maps `parentId` (items.rs:266-267) onto `translate_query`, which resolves a non-nil parent_id ONLY as `bi.\"ParentId\" = ?` (direct children) or, when recursive, via the `AncestorIds` closure (translate_query.rs:169-184). Neither surfaces box-set membership: a collection's members are ordinary movies whose real `ParentId` is their library folder, and their box-set link lives exclusively in the `LinkedChildren` table (written by `upsert_linked_child`, which never touches `AncestorIds`). There is NO BoxSet-parent → LinkedChildren dispatch anywhere in the query path (item_repository.rs / translate_query.rs), and it is explicitly documented as deferred at items.rs:209-211 ('the box-set/collection-type dispatch ... that need the un-ported Folder OOP tree are deferred'). Consequently box-set members are invisible through the browse path both before AND after the DELETE, so the harness observes no delta (H=False). Jellyfin merges LinkedChildren into BoxSet.GetChildren, so its read-back shows the item present-then-gone (J=True).
proposed_fix: none needed for the DELETE itself — the write is correct and tested. The observed non-parity is the deferred BoxSet-children browse path. Closing it (a separate, larger task, not this op) means: in translate_query/item_repository, when the parent_id resolves to a BoxSet (or more generally a folder whose children come from LinkedChildren), UNION the manual `LinkedChildren` members into the non-recursive parentId result (SELECT ChildId FROM LinkedChildren WHERE ParentId = ? AND ChildType = 0), matching Jellyfin's Folder.GetChildren which merges LinkedChildren. Only after that read path exists will the DELETE's effect become observable through the standard browse and diff clean against Jellyfin.
faithfulness: Jellyfin's CollectionController.RemoveFromCollection removes the item from the BoxSet's LinkedChildren (CollectionManager.RemoveFromCollection). A box set's contents are read back via GET /Items?parentId={boxSetId}, where ItemsController resolves the BoxSet as a Folder and returns Folder.GetChildren — which merges the LinkedChildren edges. So Jellyfin shows the member present before and absent after (J=True). Hermit deletes the same edge but never exposes it through the parentId browse, so the effect is real in the DB yet unobservable via the standard read (H=False).
collision_risk: translate_query.rs (parent_id branch) and item_repository.rs get_items path — hot query-building code shared by all /Items browses; a BoxSet-children UNION touches the core query builder.
verify: Manager-level effect already proven: `cargo nextest run -p hermit-core create_collection_persists_row_and_members` (asserts get_collections_containing_item empties after remove). To prove the harness-observable parity once the read path is added: over HTTP, POST /Collections then POST /Collections/{id}/Items ids=A,B; GET /Items?parentId={id} returns [A,B]; DELETE /Collections/{id}/Items?ids=A; GET /Items?parentId={id} returns [B] — currently returns [] both times, which is why the effect is unconfirmed.

root_cause: GUID-format mismatch between the id Hermit hands the client and the id it compares in the DB. GetPlaylistItems emits PlaylistItemId dashless: `dto.playlist_item_id = Some(item.id.replace('-', ""))` (playlists.rs:280) — matching Jellyfin's Guid.ToString("N"). A client (and the differential harness) reads that dashless id and sends it back as `entryIds`. But `remove_item_from_playlist` binds that dashless string straight into `DELETE FROM "LinkedChildren" WHERE "ParentId"=?1 AND "ChildId"=?2` (collection_manager.rs:554-563), while ChildId was stored in canonical DASHED form via `child_id.to_string()` in upsert_linked_child (linked_children_service.rs:237). Dashless != dashed, so the DELETE matches zero rows and the playlist count is unchanged (H=False). The comment at collection_manager.rs:553 ("Entry ids are approximated by the child item id") documents the ChildId==entry design, but overlooks that the emitted id is dashless while the stored ChildId is dashed. move_item has the identical mismatch (collection_manager.rs:580-591): it looks for the dashless entry_id inside a dashed ChildId order list, finds no position, and returns Ok(()) as a silent no-op.
proposed_fix: Normalize each entry_id to the canonical dashed GUID before comparing against the stored ChildId. In remove_item_from_playlist (collection_manager.rs:554), parse the incoming entry_id: `let Ok(child) = Uuid::parse_str(entry_id) else { continue }; ... .bind(child.to_string())`. Uuid::parse_str accepts both dashed and dashless forms, and .to_string() yields the canonical dashed format the DB actually stores, so it round-trips regardless of which form the client sends. Apply the same normalization in move_item (collection_manager.rs:589) — compare `order.iter().position(|c| Uuid::parse_str(c).ok() == Uuid::parse_str(entry_id).ok())` or normalize entry_id up front. (Alternative, equally valid: keep the DELETE binding as-is but stop dashless-stripping at playlists.rs:280 so the emitted PlaylistItemId stays dashed to match ChildId — but that would diverge from Jellyfin's "N" format on the wire, so normalizing at the DB comparison is the faithful choice.)
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin (PlaylistsController.RemoveItemFromPlaylist → PlaylistManager.RemoveFromPlaylistAsync) emits PlaylistItemId as Guid.ToString("N") (dashless) AND resolves the passed entryIds against LinkedChild ids using the same normalized comparison, so the dashless id round-trips and the entry is removed. Hermit already matches the emitted-id format (dashless at playlists.rs:280) but breaks the round-trip by comparing that dashless value against a dashed stored ChildId. Fix restores the round-trip Jellyfin guarantees.
collision_risk: library_manager.rs (none directly); the fix touches collection_manager.rs (remove_item_from_playlist + move_item) and the DTO emission in playlists.rs handler — moderate: entry-id addressing is also used by the Move op and its tests
verify: Add/extend a hermit-core test in collection_manager.rs (mirroring get_playlist_items_returns_members at line 749): create a playlist, add an item, read PlaylistItemId as the DTO returns it (dashless via item.id.replace('-',"")), call remove_item_from_playlist with that dashless string, then re-query get_playlist_items and assert the list is empty. Before the fix this stays non-empty (reproduces H=False); after, it is empty. Then `cargo nextest run -p hermit-core collection_manager`.

root_cause: The Intro Skipper plugin is a compiled-in extension in Hermit (see handlers::intro_skipper and the REAL_ROUTES comment block at crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/mod.rs:664-679). Hermit ships its five controllers as first-class routes, so GET /IntroSkipper/SupportBundle resolves to support_bundle() and returns 200 with a plain-text bundle. The differential reference is STOCK Jellyfin 10.11.8, which has no IntroSkipper plugin installed, so it 404s. The harness reports H=200 J=404 and mislabels it "schema-invalid," but the route is fully in the vendored OpenAPI contract (contracts/jellyfin-openapi-10.11.8.json:48022) with a 200 text/plain string schema — exactly what Hermit returns. No diverging fields (DIVERGING FIELDS: []). This is a Hermit-by-design compiled-in extension route that stock Jellyfin lacks, not a bug or schema violation.
proposed_fix: none needed — Hermit's 200 text/plain response conforms to the vendored spec's GetSupportBundle definition. The J=404 is because the differential reference is stock Jellyfin without the IntroSkipper plugin, so the delta is expected-extension noise, not a contract or schema divergence. The "schema-invalid" flag is a harness artifact of comparing against a server that lacks the plugin.
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin only exposes this route when the IntroSkipper (Intro Skipper / jellyfin-plugin-intro-skipper) plugin is installed; its TroubleshootingController.GetSupportBundle returns a plain-text Markdown support bundle (server/plugin version, OS, fpcalc presence). Hermit faithfully ports that controller and content type. The vendored 10.11.8 contract includes the route with a 200 text/plain string schema, which Hermit matches.
verify: grep confirms route in contract; curl returns 200 text/plain bundle

root_cause: Hermit's `QueryFilters` DTO carries two fields that do not exist on Jellyfin's type — `AudioLanguages` and `SubtitleLanguages` — and the `/Items/Filters2` handler (`get_query_filters`) actively populates them by aggregating media-stream languages for video type sets (has_language_facets → get_media_stream_languages_by_type). Because these are `Vec<NameValuePair>` (not `Option`), serde always serializes them (as `[]` when empty), so every Filters2 response includes two extra keys. Real Jellyfin 10.11.8 `QueryFilters` has ONLY `Genres` and `Tags`, and `FilterController.GetQueryFilters` sets only `Genres`. The vendored spec's `QueryFilters` schema declares exactly `{Genres, Tags}` with `additionalProperties: false`, so Hermit's output is schema-invalid. The code comment claiming this ports `FilterController.GetQueryFilters` is inaccurate — the C# controller never computes languages (the DTO has no such fields). This is a Hermit fabrication, not fixture poverty or instance noise.
proposed_fix: Remove the two non-contract fields from the DTO and stop populating them. In crates/hermit-model/src/querying/filters.rs delete the `audio_languages` and `subtitle_languages` fields (lines 19-23) so `QueryFilters` = `{genres, tags}` matching Jellyfin. In crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/filter.rs delete the entire language-facet block (lines 239-265) and the now-unused helpers `has_language_facets` (152-165) and `language_pairs` (166-175), plus the now-unused imports (MediaStreamType, NameValuePair) and the `get_media_stream_languages_by_type` call site. If `get_media_stream_languages_by_type` on the library manager has no other callers, it can also be removed from hermit-traits/hermit-core, but that is optional cleanup, not required for parity. Leaving `tags` empty is fine — Jellyfin's Filters2 also leaves Tags at its default.
faithfulness: Jellyfin 10.11.8 `MediaBrowser.Model.Querying.QueryFilters` defines exactly two properties, `NameGuidPair[] Genres` and `string[] Tags`; `Jellyfin.Api.Controllers.FilterController.GetQueryFilters` sets only `filters.Genres` (via GetGenres/GetMusicGenres) and returns. It never reads media streams or computes audio/subtitle languages. The vendored OpenAPI QueryFilters schema is `{Genres, Tags}` with additionalProperties:false. After the fix Hermit emits only Genres (and an empty Tags), matching both the spec and the C# behavior.
collision_risk: low (touches querying/filters.rs and handlers/filter.rs; does not touch dto_service.rs / media_source_manager.rs / entities_media.rs / library_manager.rs, though the optional trait-method removal would touch library_manager)
verify: After the change: `curl -s "http://localhost:8096/Items/Filters2?includeItemTypes=Movie" -H "$AUTH" | jq 'keys'` should return only ["Genres","Tags"] (no AudioLanguages/SubtitleLanguages). Also `cargo nextest run -p hermit-api` and the contract-superset test stay green; a schema-validation check against components.schemas.QueryFilters (additionalProperties:false) now passes.

root_cause: The handler crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/suggestions.rs:58-91 is a faithful port of Jellyfin's SuggestionsController.GetSuggestions: it builds an InternalItemsQuery with order_by = [(ItemSortBy::Random, SortOrder::Descending)], is_virtual_item=Some(false), recursive=true, and the same media_types/include_item_types/paging/enable_total_record_count semantics. The "+whole-item set membership" divergence is therefore inherent: with Random ordering, two independently-scanned servers over the same 500 synthetic movies return a different random subset/order every call, and the harness aligns by Path so a random page never contains the same items — this is pure randomness + independent-scan id noise, not a logic difference. The "schema-invalid" flag is not Suggestions-specific: the wrapper QueryResult<BaseItemDto> serializes only Items/TotalRecordCount/StartIndex (all valid vs BaseItemDtoQueryResult). The only additionalProperties:false violation possible comes from the SHARED BaseItemDto, which carries two Hermit-only fields absent from the 10.11.8 spec — OriginalLanguage (base_item.rs:512) and AlbumNormalizationGain (base_item.rs:506). Both are skip_serializing_if=Option::is_none and are unpopulated for metadata-less synthetic movies, so they don't actually appear in these responses, and if they did they would flag EVERY item-returning endpoint (/Items, /Users/{id}/Items, etc.), not Suggestions alone. So the schema-invalid mark is a harness artifact of validating a shared DTO against the strict spec, not a defect in this op.
proposed_fix: none needed for the Suggestions op itself — the item-set divergence is caused by ItemSortBy::Random plus independent scans and is expected. Separately (NOT a Suggestions bug, a latent global schema-conformance nit shared by all item DTOs): BaseItemDto carries two fields not in the 10.11.8 contract — OriginalLanguage (base_item.rs:512) and AlbumNormalizationGain (base_item.rs:506) — under a schema that declares additionalProperties:false. They are skip-if-none so harmless on empty fixtures, but a strict validator would reject any response that populates them. If exact wire conformance is desired, drop or feature-gate these two fields; but this belongs to a BaseItemDto conformance sweep, not this operation.
faithfulness: Jellyfin's SuggestionsController.GetSuggestions runs GetItemsResult with OrderBy=[(ItemSortBy.Random, SortOrder.Descending)], IsVirtualItem=false, Recursive=true, and returns QueryResult<BaseItemDto> with TotalRecordCount coalesced from EnableTotalRecordCount (default false). Hermit matches this exactly, including the random ordering that makes the returned set non-deterministic by design. The response type BaseItemDtoQueryResult (Items/TotalRecordCount/StartIndex) also matches.
collision_risk: low for the Suggestions op; the optional BaseItemDto field cleanup would touch entities_media.rs-adjacent dto_service.rs and base_item.rs (hot: dto_service.rs) and would affect all item endpoints, so defer it to a dedicated DTO conformance pass rather than bundling with this op
verify: Call GET /Items/Suggestions twice against one Hermit instance: the returned Items set/order differs between calls, confirming Random ordering is the source of set-membership divergence (deterministic diff impossible by design). To confirm no Suggestions-specific extra field: `curl .../Items/Suggestions | jq '.Items[0] | keys'` returns only spec-valid keys for synthetic movies (OriginalLanguage/AlbumNormalizationGain absent because unpopulated). To confirm the two extras are global-not-Suggestions: grep base_item.rs for original_language/album_normalization_gain and note skip_serializing_if=Option::is_none.

root_cause: The flagged fields split into two buckets. (1) SCHEMA-INVALID + Hermit-extra: `MediaStream.is_original` is a non-Option `bool` (crates/hermit-model/src/entities_media.rs:504) that always serializes as `"IsOriginal": true|false`. But `IsOriginal` does NOT exist in the vendored 10.11.8 MediaStream schema at all (`jq '.components.schemas.MediaStream.properties | has("IsOriginal")'` -> false; it was added post-10.11.8). Hermit emits a field the contract forbids -> the "schema-invalid" flag and "IsOriginal Hermit-extra". (2) MediaSource/MediaStream MISSING fields: `HermitMediaSourceManager::static_source` (crates/hermit-core/src/media_source_manager.rs:158-177) builds the MediaSourceInfo with `..Default::default()`, so the source-level `Bitrate`, `DefaultAudioStreamIndex`, `ETag`, and `VideoType` are left None while Jellyfin computes each (VideoType=VideoFile for a video file, Bitrate summed/estimated from streams, DefaultAudioStreamIndex from the default audio stream, ETag from the item). Note the DTO-level video_type IS set (dto_service.rs:959) but the per-source VideoType is not. Separately, `LocalizedDefault`/`LocalizedExternal` are only consumed to compute display_title in entities_media.rs and are never assigned onto the serialized MediaStream, so they stay None where Jellyfin populates them from its localization manager. CanDelete J=true H=false is a third, unconditional defect: dto_service.rs:779 hardcodes `dto.can_delete = Some(false)` (module docs admit it "collapses to a thin default" because the C# logic needs the BaseItem tree). The remaining stream-probe fields (BitRate, IsAVC, Level, RealFrameRate) are actually fully wired end-to-end (schema column, entity field, ffprobe parse at probe_result_normalizer.rs:283/373-376, and stream_to_dto mapping), so they populate on a real Hermit scan of the identical fixture clip; their appearance in the diff is independent-scan/probe-value noise (two ffmpeg builds probing the same 5fps clip; e.g. RealFrameRate float rounding), not a code gap.
proposed_fix: Three surgical fixes. (A) Stop emitting IsOriginal: either drop `is_original` from MediaStream or, to keep the internal display_title logic, mark it non-serializing with `#[serde(skip)]` (and remove the round-trip in stream_dto_to_entity/stream_to_dto if the column is dropped) so the response matches the 10.11.8 contract. (B) In static_source (media_source_manager.rs:162) populate the source-level fields Jellyfin computes: video_type = Some(VideoType::VideoFile) for a video item; default_audio_stream_index from the first is_default audio stream (else first audio) in `streams`; bitrate = sum of stream bit_rates when all present, else estimate from size/run_time_ticks; e_tag from the item (Jellyfin uses BaseItem.GetEtag hash) or at minimum the item id/date-modified hash. (C) For CanDelete, port Jellyfin's Folder/Video CanDelete: a non-virtual library item with a real file location that the user is allowed to delete returns true; return `Some(!item.is_virtual_item && user_can_delete)` rather than the hardcoded false at dto_service.rs:779. Also set localized_default/localized_external (and forced/undefined/hearing_impaired) on each MediaStream from the localization strings before serialization so those fields are present like Jellyfin.
faithfulness: Jellyfin 10.11.8 MediaStream schema has no IsOriginal property, so a faithful response must not emit it. Jellyfin's MediaSourceManager.GetStaticMediaSources sets MediaSourceInfo.VideoType=VideoFile, DefaultAudioStreamIndex, Bitrate (InferTotalBitrate / stream sum), and ETag; DtoService populates the Localized* labels via ILocalizationManager. BaseItem.CanDelete returns true for a real, non-virtual library file the user may delete. The wired probe fields (IsAVC/Level/RealFrameRate/BitRate) already mirror ffprobe r_frame_rate/level/bit_rate faithfully.
collision_risk: dto_service.rs (CanDelete + localized labels), media_source_manager.rs (static_source source-level fields), entities_media.rs (is_original serde) - all hot files named in the schema
verify: Scan the fixture into Hermit, then `curl -s .../Items/{movieId}?fields=MediaSources,MediaStreams,CanDelete | jq '.MediaSources[0] | {Bitrate,DefaultAudioStreamIndex,ETag,VideoType}, .CanDelete, (.MediaStreams[] | has("IsOriginal"))'` and assert VideoType=="VideoFile", Bitrate/DefaultAudioStreamIndex/ETag non-null, CanDelete==true, and no MediaStream has an IsOriginal key. Add an rstest asserting serialized MediaStream JSON contains no "IsOriginal" and static_source stamps VideoType/DefaultAudioStreamIndex.

root_cause:
The Ancestors set diverges for two independent reasons, both traceable to Hermit deliberately not materializing the synthetic library-root tree.

(1) Set-membership gap (the missing:10 = 2 per item): Jellyfin's LibraryController.GetAncestors walks item.GetParent() until null, yielding for a Movie: CollectionFolder -> UserRootFolder ("Media Folders") -> AggregateFolder ("Root"). Hermit never creates a UserRootFolder or AggregateFolder row. In library_scan.rs the movie is parented directly to the CollectionFolder (base_item(..., cf, cf, ...) sets parent_id = top_parent_id = cf, library_scan.rs:700), and virtual_folder_manager.rs ensure_collection_folder (:140-150) creates the CollectionFolder row with NO parent_id. So get_ancestors' ParentId-chain walk (hermit-traits/src/library.rs:175-203, faithful port of BaseItem.GetParents) terminates at the CollectionFolder and returns exactly one ancestor, whereas Jellyfin returns the CollectionFolder plus the two synthetic root folders above it. get_user_root_folder (library.rs:216) resolves a UserRootFolder row only if one was persisted; nothing in the scan/boot path ever persists one (grep confirms UserRootFolder/AggregateFolder appear only in item_type_lookup name tables, kinds.rs, and tests).

(2) CollectionFolder id mismatch (the extra:5 + the remaining missing): item ids are path-derived MD5 (item_type_lookup.rs:197-200, key = TypeFullName + lowercased path, port of GetNewItemIdInternal). The CollectionFolder's path is its virtual-folder directory under the container data-dir, which is /config in Jellyfin vs /data in Hermit. Different path -> different MD5 -> the one CollectionFolder ancestor Hermit does return cannot align by id with Jellyfin's, so it is scored as extra on Hermit's side and missing on Jellyfin's side. This is pure container-instance noise (/config vs /data), not a bug.

Reason (2) is instance noise; reason (1) is a genuine-but-by-design structural gap (Hermit intentionally omits the UserRootFolder/AggregateFolder tree, documented as "out of scope for this portable seam" at library.rs:210-215). The differential harness cannot distinguish these because it aligns by Path and every synthetic root folder's path also differs by data-dir.
proposed_fix:
none needed for the differential-harness flag itself: the extra:5 is /config-vs-/data path-derived id noise, and the missing:10 is Hermit's deliberate omission of the synthetic UserRootFolder/AggregateFolder tree (get_user_root_folder is documented out-of-scope). No handler/DTO logic is wrong: the handler (items.rs:478) and the ParentId walk (library.rs:175-203) faithfully mirror LibraryController.GetAncestors + BaseItem.GetParents given the persisted tree.

If full ancestor parity is later desired (this is the deferred-subsystem edge): during boot/scan, materialize a single UserRootFolder ("Media Folders") and AggregateFolder ("Root") row, set each CollectionFolder's parent_id to the UserRootFolder (ensure_collection_folder, virtual_folder_manager.rs:140), and chain UserRootFolder.parent_id -> AggregateFolder. Then the existing walk would emit CollectionFolder -> UserRootFolder -> AggregateFolder automatically, matching Jellyfin. That is an L-effort library-tree change, not an Ancestors-endpoint change, and should only be done if the root-folder tree is wanted globally (it also affects /Items/Root, UserViews, and item-count roll-ups).
faithfulness: Jellyfin's LibraryController.GetAncestors walks BaseItem.GetParent() to null, adding every non-null parent as a BaseItemDto (TranslateParentItem only rewrites, never drops, UserRootFolder/AggregateFolder when a userId is supplied). For a Movie in a library the real chain is CollectionFolder -> UserRootFolder ("Media Folders", fixed synthetic id) -> AggregateFolder ("Root"), so Jellyfin returns ~3 ancestors. Hermit's walk is itself faithful; it just runs over a tree that lacks the two synthetic root folders, so it returns only the CollectionFolder.
collision_risk: low (library_manager.rs / virtual_folder_manager.rs / library_scan.rs if the root-folder tree is ever built; no change to dto_service.rs or media_source_manager.rs)
verify: Scan a library into Hermit, then curl GET /Items/{movieId}/Ancestors: today it returns a single-element array containing the CollectionFolder. Confirm the CollectionFolder id equals derive_item_id(CollectionFolder, <virtual-folder path>) and that the path embeds the data-dir (/data), proving the cross-instance id difference is path-driven. Grep confirms no UserRootFolder/AggregateFolder row is ever persisted outside tests (rg 'UserRootFolder|AggregateFolder' crates/hermit-core/src apps/hermit-server/src, excluding tests and name tables, yields nothing).

root_cause: The handler `get_item_image_infos` projects image rows via `image_info_dto`, which hardcodes `image_tag: None` (crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/images.rs:473) with a comment claiming the image-processor cache tag "is not yet ported." That claim is stale: the cache tag IS fully ported. `ImageProcessor::get_image_cache_tag` (crates/hermit-drawing/src/processor.rs:460-481) computes md5(path + .NET-ticks) as 32-char lowercase hex, and DtoService already uses it to populate `BaseItemDto.ImageTags` (crates/hermit-core/src/dto_service.rs:435-441, 654-665). Jellyfin's `ImageController.GetItemImageInfos` calls `GetImageCacheTag(item, image)` per image and sets `ImageInfo.ImageTag`. Hermit's endpoint simply never calls the (available) processor: `state.image_processor` is present in AppState (crates/hermit-api/src/state.rs:72) and already used on the serve path (images.rs:204), and `ItemImageInfo` carries `path` + `date_modified` (the exact inputs the tag needs). So every image on every item returns ImageTag=null here while Jellyfin returns the md5 tag. This is not fixture poverty — the 500 synthetic movies each have a Primary poster with a real path+mtime, so the tag would compute.
proposed_fix: Compute the tag in the handler instead of stubbing it. Make `project_image_infos` (and the `image_info_dto` it calls) take `&Option<Arc<dyn ImageProcessor>>` and `item_id`, and become async. For each image, when a processor is present call `processor.get_image_cache_tag(item_id, image).await.ok().flatten()` and set that as `image_tag` (mirroring DtoService::image_tag at dto_service.rs:435-441, which tolerates errors by mapping to None). Then in `get_item_image_infos` (images.rs:406-412) pass `&state.image_processor` through: `Ok(axum::Json(project_image_infos(item_id, &state.image_processor, &images).await))`. Delete the stale comment at images.rs:471-472. When `state.image_processor` is None (transcode/drawing disabled), leaving ImageTag None is acceptable and matches the existing "processor absent" degradation used on the serve path.
faithfulness: Jellyfin's ImageController.GetItemImageInfos sets ImageInfo.ImageTag = _imageProcessor.GetImageCacheTag(item, image) for each stored image. The tag is md5(item.Path-for-the-image + imageDateModified.Ticks) formatted as ToString("N") (32 lowercase hex, no dashes). Hermit's get_image_cache_tag_for_path already implements exactly this (processor.rs:471-481), so the resulting tag will byte-match Jellyfin's for identical path+mtime.
collision_risk: low — the change is confined to crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/images.rs (project_image_infos/image_info_dto/get_item_image_infos); it only reads existing dto_service.rs / processor.rs machinery, does not modify hot files dto_service.rs / media_source_manager.rs / entities_media.rs / library_manager.rs.
verify: Unit: add an rstest in images.rs asserting project_image_infos with a fake ImageProcessor (like the dto_service tests' fake returning "tag:{path}") yields image_tag = Some for a Primary image and that md5(path+ticks) matches processor output. Live: scan a movie with a poster into Hermit, then `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8096/Items/{id}/Images | jq '.[0].ImageTag'` returns a 32-char hex string, not null; compare equality against the same item's `.ImageTags.Primary` from `GET /Items/{id}` (they must be identical).

root_cause: PlaybackInfo builds each MediaSource via the SAME assembler as Items/{itemId}: MediaSourceManager::static_source (crates/hermit-core/src/media_source_manager.rs:158-177), which fills only id/path/name/container/size/run_time_ticks/streams/protocol/type/supports_* and leaves everything else at ..Default::default(). That drops four MediaSource-level fields Jellyfin always populates: (1) VideoType — Jellyfin sets VideoType.VideoFile in Video.GetMediaSources; (2) Bitrate — Jellyfin calls InferTotalBitrate() summing the stream bit_rates (Hermit even HAS MediaSourceInfo::infer_total_bitrate at media_source_info.rs:269 but never calls it); (3) DefaultAudioStreamIndex — Jellyfin runs SetDefaultAudioAndSubtitleStreamIndexes; Hermit's apply_stream_decision (media_info.rs:329) negotiates a StreamInfo but never writes source.default_audio_stream_index, and the GET form skips that path entirely; (4) ETag — Jellyfin stamps the item DTO ETag onto the source. Separately, the two MediaStream fields LocalizedDefault/LocalizedExternal are set at probe time (probe_result_normalizer.rs:311-312, 352-355) but have NO DB columns, so stream_to_dto (media_source_manager.rs:205-262) re-reads streams from the DB with these = None and serde skips them — a structural drop. The remaining flagged stream fields (BitRate, IsAVC, Level, RealFrameRate, IsOriginal) are genuine persisted columns (0001_initial.sql:447 RealFrameRate; base_items entity is_avc/level/is_original/real_frame_rate) that Hermit DOES populate from ffprobe and re-serialize; their diff on 500 synthetic movies is independent-scan probe-value noise (each server ran its own ffprobe), not a code gap.

root_cause: The flagged diff (TotalRecordCount J=16 H=12, +86 whole-item set churn) is a product of fixture poverty combined with Jellyfin's randomized tiebreak, not a reproducible correctness bug. The fixture (benchmark/gen-fixtures.sh) creates 500 movies all named "Movie NNNN (2020)" with NO genres/tags/people/studios/ratings and ALL with ProductionYear=2020. Jellyfin's LibraryController.GetSimilarItems sets SimilarTo=item and scores candidates via SqliteItemRepository.GetSimilarityScore (genres*10 + tags*10 + studios*3 + people*3 + ProductionYear proximity +2/+2/+1 + OfficialRating +2). With this fixture only the year terms fire, and they fire IDENTICALLY for every candidate (all year 2020) => every candidate ties at the same score, so Jellyfin's final `ORDER BY SimilarityScore DESC, RANDOM()` returns a RANDOM subset of the 500 movies. That non-determinism is exactly the +86 set churn and the volatile count. Hermit (crates/hermit-core/src/similar_items_manager.rs:68-97) does NOT port the weighted scorer at all — it runs a genre-overlap InternalItemsQuery ordered by CommunityRating desc; with empty genres the genre predicate is dropped entirely (translate_query.rs:650 only adds it when non-empty), so Hermit returns arbitrary same-kind movies up to its limit. Both sides are thus returning arbitrary subsets of the same pool; the divergence is fixture + methodology (differing limit param on the two probes: H default is DEFAULT_SIMILAR_LIMIT=10, similar_items_manager.rs:30), not a field Hermit gets wrong.
proposed_fix: none needed for THIS flag — the specific diff is fixture poverty + Jellyfin's RANDOM() tiebreak (Jellyfin's own result is non-reproducible here, so no fixed target exists to match). SEPARATELY (not required by this flag, and self-admitted as deferred in the file's module doc): Hermit's similar-items algorithm is a real simplification of Jellyfin's weighted GetSimilarityScore. To close the algorithm gap generally, similar_items_manager.rs:get_similar_items should port GetSimilarityScore (weighted overlap of genres/tags/people/studios + ProductionYear proximity + OfficialRating) and order by that score rather than genre-membership + CommunityRating. This needs a SimilarTo path (a scoring SELECT) added to InternalItemsQuery/translate_query since InternalItemsQuery has no SimilarTo field today. But it would NOT change the observed benchmark numbers, because the metadata-free single-year fixture makes every candidate tie.
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin: LibraryController.GetSimilarItems builds InternalItemsQuery{SimilarTo=item, IncludeItemTypes=[Movie/Series/...]}; SqliteItemRepository computes a SimilarityScore = sum of weighted metadata overlaps (genres*10, tags*10, studios*3, people*3) plus ProductionYear-proximity terms (+2 exact, +2 within 1yr, +1 within 2yr) and OfficialRating (+2), filters MinSimilarityScore, and orders by `SimilarityScore DESC, RANDOM()`. Episode/IItemByName seeds short-circuit to empty. The RANDOM() tiebreak means ties are non-deterministic — which is why a metadata-poor equal-year fixture yields a random, non-reproducible result set on the Jellyfin side.
collision_risk: low (would touch similar_items_manager.rs, translate_query.rs, and add a SimilarTo field to internal_items_query.rs if the deferred scorer is ever implemented; none of the named hot files dto_service.rs/media_source_manager.rs/entities_media.rs/library_manager.rs)

With varied metadata Jellyfin's scores diverge, RANDOM() stops dominating, and a stable expected set exists to diff against; only then can a real algorithm bug (vs the current genre-overlap-only impl) be observed and asserted. As-is, cargo nextest -p hermit-core similar_items_manager passes and the current handler is contract-correct (QueryResult with startIndex=0, TotalRecordCount=rows).

root_cause: Jellyfin's LibraryController.GetMediaFolders returns _libraryManager.GetUserRootFolder().Children — the user-root folder's children, which include the scanned library CollectionFolder(s) AND an auto-provisioned ManualPlaylistsFolder living on disk under the data dir ({DataPath}/data/playlists, shown by the harness as /config/data/playlists). Hermit's handler get_media_folders (crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/library.rs:459-480) instead delegates to state.user_views.get_user_views(), whose impl (crates/hermit-core/src/user_view_manager.rs:56-67) queries only include_item_types = [CollectionFolder, UserView]. Hermit never creates any PlaylistsFolder/ManualPlaylistsFolder item — there is no seeding of one in library_scan.rs, state.rs, or the playlist code paths — so it can never appear here. Result: Jellyfin TotalRecordCount=2 (library + Playlists), Hermit=1. The /config/data/playlists path is a data-dir folder, not a scanned-media path, so this is a genuinely missing whole item, not /config-vs-/data path noise (the +3 set-membership delta on the library folders themselves IS independent-scan GUID noise, but the Playlists folder is a real absence).
proposed_fix: Provision a Playlists media folder so it becomes a child of the user root folder and is returned by GetMediaFolders, matching Jellyfin. Concretely: (1) on server/library init, ensure a ManualPlaylistsFolder BaseItemEntity row exists with parent = the UserRootFolder ("Media Folders" root, seeded at library_manager.rs:955), Name="Playlists", Path = {data_dir}/data/playlists (mkdir it), analogous to Jellyfin's PlaylistManager.GetPlaylistsFolder. (2) Make GetMediaFolders return the user-root folder's children rather than only collection folders — either add ManualPlaylistsFolder/PlaylistsFolder to the include_item_types set in user_view_manager.rs:62, or (more faithful) give the handler a dedicated path that lists GetUserRootFolder().Children (CollectionFolder + UserView + ManualPlaylistsFolder), name-sorted. Newly created playlists should then be parented under this folder (currently they are not parented to any media folder). Because this requires seeding a new item kind and a data-dir folder plus a new repository/query path, it is more than a one-liner.
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin (LibraryController.GetMediaFolders) returns _libraryManager.GetUserRootFolder().Children ordered by SortName, optionally filtered by IsHidden when isHidden is supplied. Those children are the library CollectionFolders plus the auto-created ManualPlaylistsFolder (a real on-disk folder under the data path, kind ManualPlaylistsFolder/CollectionType=playlists). The fix should make Hermit expose the same Playlists folder as a user-root child so both servers agree on the folder set and TotalRecordCount.

root_cause: Hermit's `VirtualFolderManager::get_virtual_folders` (crates/hermit-core/src/virtual_folder_manager.rs:375-382) builds each `VirtualFolderInfo` with `..VirtualFolderInfo::default()`, leaving `refresh_status` (and `refresh_progress`) as `None`. The DTO field `refresh_status: Option<String>` has `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` (crates/hermit-model/src/entities_media.rs:349-350), so a `None` is omitted from the JSON entirely. Jellyfin's `LibraryStructureController.GetVirtualFolders` calls `_libraryManager.GetVirtualFolders(true)` (includeRefreshState=true), and `GetVirtualFolderInfo` then always assigns `info.RefreshStatus = RefreshProgress.HasValue ? "Active" : refreshQueue.Contains(id) ? "Queued" : "Idle";` — so at rest every folder reports `RefreshStatus="Idle"`, never absent. Hence the differential harness sees RefreshStatus present on Jellyfin and missing on Hermit. This is a genuine parity gap, not fixture poverty or /config-vs-/data noise (the field is unconditionally emitted regardless of library contents).
proposed_fix: In `get_virtual_folders` (virtual_folder_manager.rs:375), populate `refresh_status`. Faithful port: query the provider manager's refresh queue (the trait method already exists — `ProviderManager::get_refresh_queue` at hermit-traits/src/providers.rs:285) once before the loop, and for each folder compute status like Jellyfin: `Active` if a per-folder refresh progress is known, else `Queued` if the folder's item_id is in the refresh queue, else `Idle`. Minimum faithful change (Hermit has no per-folder refresh-progress tracking yet, so the `Active` branch is unreachable today): set `refresh_status: Some(if queue.contains(&item_id) { "Queued" } else { "Idle" }.to_string())`, and `refresh_progress` stays `None` until scan-progress plumbing exists. If wiring the queue into VirtualFolderManager is out of scope for this pass, the smaller correct default that matches Jellyfin's at-rest output is `refresh_status: Some("Idle".to_string())`. Do not touch the serde skip attribute — Jellyfin's own field is nullable; the fix is to stop leaving it None.
faithfulness: Jellyfin (v10.11.8) LibraryManager.GetVirtualFolderInfo, invoked via GetVirtualFolders(true) from the controller, always sets RefreshStatus to one of "Active"/"Queued"/"Idle" (never null) and RefreshProgress only when a refresh is active. At rest with no scan running, every VirtualFolderInfo carries RefreshStatus="Idle".

root_cause: Jellyfin's LiveTvController.GetSchedulesDirectCountries is an unconditional HTTP passthrough: `File(await client.GetStreamAsync("https://json.schedulesdirect.org/20141201/available/countries"), MediaTypeNames.Application.Json)` — it streams Schedules Direct's live country JSON (a region-keyed object like {"North America":[...],"Europe":[...]}) regardless of whether any SD provider is configured. Hermit has no Schedules Direct provider at all (grep for SchedulesDirect/json.schedulesdirect across hermit-core and hermit-livetv returns nothing); its Live TV is M3U+XMLTV only. The handler at crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/live_tv.rs:292-296 hardcodes Json(serde_json::json!([])), returning an empty JSON array. The harness flags 'schema-invalid' because the vendored spec declares the 200 body as type:string, format:binary (a raw File() stream), which a JSON validator won't cleanly match for EITHER server's body — but the substantive divergence is that Hermit returns [] where Jellyfin returns a populated country dictionary. Not fixture poverty or instance noise: real Jellyfin fetches the same upstream on every call, independent of the scanned library.
proposed_fix: To reach parity the handler must proxy the upstream: fetch https://json.schedulesdirect.org/20141201/available/countries via an HTTP client and stream the body back with content-type application/json (mirroring C#'s File(stream, "application/json")), rather than returning []. The return shape is also wrong — Jellyfin returns a region-keyed OBJECT, not an array, so [] is mis-shaped as well as empty. This belongs to the deferred Schedules Direct DVR subsystem; even a minimal version is a live-network passthrough (external dependency on json.schedulesdirect.org), which the project's no-fake-subsystem rule and offline-test posture make a real subsystem decision, not a one-liner. If SD DVR is intentionally out of scope, the current empty response is a conscious deferral rather than an accidental bug — but it does NOT match Jellyfin, which returns the country list unconditionally. proposed_fix if pursued: replace the hardcoded array with a reqwest GET of the SD countries URL, streamed through as application/json.
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin's LiveTvController.GetSchedulesDirectCountries streams https://json.schedulesdirect.org/20141201/available/countries verbatim to the client as application/json (File(GetStreamAsync(...), 'application/json')). It requires NO configured SD provider — a pure upstream proxy — so stock Jellyfin returns a populated region-keyed country object. The fix should match this: proxy the same URL and stream the body with content-type application/json.
verify: Network-enabled: curl -s -H 'Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=...' http://localhost:8096/LiveTv/ListingProviders/SchedulesDirect/Countries | jq 'type' should print 'object' (region-keyed dict) matching curl -s https://json.schedulesdirect.org/20141201/available/countries | jq 'type', instead of today's [] (array). Offline: assert the handler forwards the upstream stream rather than emitting a fixed array.

root_cause: Hermit's port of GetMovieRecommendations ignores Jellyfin's seed-selection filters. Jellyfin (SimilarItemsManager.GetMovieRecommendationsAsync, lines 250-315) builds categories only from: (1) recentlyPlayedMovies — an InternalItemsQuery with IsPlayed=true ordered by DatePlayed (requires playback history); (2) likedMovies — IsFavoriteOrLiked=true (requires favorites); (3) director/actor categories from people metadata on those played movies. With the synthetic fixture (no playback history, no favorites, no people, no genres), all 6 category enumerators yield nothing, the round-robin while-loop hits allEmpty and breaks, so Jellyfin returns 0. Hermit's similar_items_manager.rs:99-138 instead seeds from the parent's most-recently-CREATED movies (ItemSortBy::DateCreated, with NO is_played / is_favorite filter), then for each seed calls get_similar_items. get_similar_items (lines 68-97) filters by shared genres, but when the seed has no genres genres_of() returns empty and translate_query.rs:650 skips the genre WHERE clause entirely — so it returns all other movies of the same kind. Result: each of the top 5 recently-created movies becomes a non-empty SimilarToRecentlyPlayed category → 5 recommendations.
proposed_fix: Rewrite get_movie_recommendations (similar_items_manager.rs:99) to mirror the C# seed gating. At minimum: change the seed queries so the SimilarToRecentlyPlayed category is seeded from an InternalItemsQuery with is_played=Some(true) and order_by DatePlayed (not DateCreated), and add a SimilarToLikedItem category seeded from is_favorite_or_liked=Some(true), and add HasDirectorFromRecentlyPlayed / HasActorFromRecentlyPlayed categories derived from people on those played movies (is_movie=Some(true), is_played=Some(false), Person filter). Preserve the round-robin category assembly (double-weighting SimilarToRecentlyPlayed and SimilarToLikedItem, cap at category_limit=5, final OrderBy RecommendationType). All the needed query fields already exist in translate_query.rs (is_played:588, is_favorite_or_liked:581, is_movie:130); the fix is to USE them instead of the current DateCreated-only seed. This makes the empty fixture yield 0 categories, matching Jellyfin. Effort is L because the director/actor categories need people-name lookup (Jellyfin's GetPeopleNamesByItems) which must be verified to exist on the repository seam.
faithfulness: Jellyfin only recommends movies derived from the user's actual behavior/metadata: recently PLAYED movies (IsPlayed=true), favorited/liked movies (IsFavoriteOrLiked=true), and directors/actors of those played movies. When there is no watch history, no favorites, and no people metadata (exactly the synthetic-fixture case) it returns an empty list. Recommendations are never seeded off mere catalog membership or recency-of-import.
collision_risk: low (similar_items_manager.rs is not one of the hot files; may touch item_repository/translate_query indirectly for a people-names lookup)
verify: Unit test in similar_items_manager.rs: seed several movies with no user data (no played, no favorite, no people/genres) and assert get_movie_recommendations returns an empty Vec; then mark one movie IsPlayed and give it a genre shared by another and assert exactly one SimilarToRecentlyPlayed category appears. End-to-end: against the 500-movie fixture with no playback, GET /Movies/Recommendations must return [] (length 0) to match Jellyfin.

root_cause: Hermit does not port Jellyfin's weighted "SimilarTo" similarity scorer. Jellyfin's LibraryController.GetSimilarItems builds an InternalItemsQuery with SimilarTo=item and the DB scores each candidate by a weighted overlap of genres, tags, people, studios, official rating, and production-year proximity, returning only items with score>0 ordered by descending score. Hermit's HermitSimilarItemsManager::get_similar_items (similar_items_manager.rs:68-97) instead runs a plain genre-overlap query ordered by CommunityRating with a fixed default limit of 10 (DEFAULT_SIMILAR_LIMIT). InternalItemsQuery has no SimilarTo field at all — the weighted scorer is explicitly noted deferred in the manager's own doc comment ("The full weighted scorer (tag/person/studio/year terms) is noted deferred"). Under the synthetic fixtures every movie is named "Movie NNNN (2020)" with identical year, no genres, no ratings, no people (benchmark/gen-fixtures.sh:33-35). So (a) Jellyfin's year term makes every other movie score>0, yielding 16; (b) Hermit's filter.genres is empty, so append_item_value_predicates (translate_query.rs:650) skips the genre predicate and the query degrades to "any same-kind movie ordered by CommunityRating (all null -> arbitrary order), limited", yielding a different count (12) and a different subset (the +90 set-membership delta). The /Items/{itemId}/Similar divergence is the identical code path ("same as Items Similar").
proposed_fix: none needed for a byte-parity fix under these fixtures. The real work is a deferred subsystem: port Jellyfin's weighted similarity scorer. That means adding a SimilarTo (Uuid) field to InternalItemsQuery and implementing the scoring SQL/ordering in translate_query.rs that awards weighted points for shared genres, tags, people, studios, official rating, and production-year proximity, filters to score>0, and orders by descending score (matching Emby.Server.Implementations/Data BaseItemRepository GetSimilarityScore). Then HermitSimilarItemsManager::get_similar_items should set query.similar_to=Some(item_id) instead of the genre-only overlap + CommunityRating sort. Even after that, exact set/count parity against an independent Jellyfin scan is not guaranteed on metadata-identical fixtures (all candidates tie on score, so tiebreak ordering and limit differences remain). Recommend deprioritizing until fixtures carry real genres/years/people, or verifying against a real-metadata library.
faithfulness: Jellyfin computes similarity via a weighted multi-term overlap scorer (GetSimilarityScore over genres, tags, people/actors, studios, official rating, and production-year proximity), returns only candidates with a positive score, and orders by that score descending; production year alone contributes points, which is why metadata-poor items still yield a non-empty ranked set. The fix should reproduce that scoring and score>0 filter rather than a genre-equality filter with a rating sort.
collision_risk: low (would touch translate_query.rs query-building and add a field to internal_items_query.rs; not the named hot DTO/media-source files)
verify: Once a real weighted scorer with SimilarTo is added, unit-test in similar_items_manager.rs: seed movies sharing only production year (no genres) and assert the seed's same-year peers are returned ranked (score>0), proving year proximity alone yields similar items like Jellyfin. For the current state, the divergence is reproduced by the parity harness on synthetic fixtures (identical-year, genreless movies) and is expected given the deferred scorer.

root_cause: The `/Search/Hints` handler and `HermitSearchManager` are faithful and NOT the cause. The search issues an `InternalItemsQuery` with `name_contains="a"`, `recursive=true`, no `include_item_types`, all category `include_*` flags defaulting to true (crates/hermit-core/src/search_manager.rs:66-103). translate_query's base WHERE is only `bi.Id <> placeholder AND (bi.CleanName LIKE '%a%' OR bi.OriginalTitle LIKE '%a%')` — no implicit IsFolder/IsVirtualItem/library-ancestor restriction (translate_query.rs:72, 425-447, 542-549). Genres ARE materialized as browsable `BaseItems` rows (Type='Genre', Name=<genre>, CleanName=<clean>) sharing the ItemValueId, via save_item_values (item_persistence_service.rs:247-261, by_name_type_name maps 2→'Genre'). So IF a Genre 'Action' row exists, this search WOULD return it and score() would keep it (name 'Action' contains 'a'). Therefore H=0 means the Genre 'Action' row was never materialized — because Hermit never scanned any genre metadata for the item. Genre metadata reaches an item only from (a) a local NFO (xbmc parser DOES parse <genre>, providers/src/xbmc/base_parser.rs:441) or (b) TMDB enrichment (library_scan.rs:391 fetch_remote_metadata). TMDB/MusicBrainz are compile-time feature-gated OFF (hermit-providers/Cargo.toml:20 default omits `tmdb`/`musicbrainz`), and fetch_remote_metadata early-returns when tmdb is None. Real Jellyfin ships its TMDB/OMDb providers enabled by default, so it enriched the movie(s) with genre 'Action' and created a Genre item; Hermit, with remote providers gated off (and no NFO carrying the genre in this fixture), materialized no Genre item, so the name-contains search has nothing to match. The single divergence is a downstream metadata-availability gap, not a search defect.
proposed_fix: none needed — /Search/Hints is correct. The genre hint is missing only because no genre metadata was scanned into the item: Hermit's remote metadata providers (TMDB/MusicBrainz) are feature-gated off by default (deferred subsystem), and this fixture carried no NFO genre for the local provider to parse. Enable the `tmdb` feature (or scan media with NFO <genre> tags) and the same Genre 'Action' by-name item is materialized and returned by the identical search path, restoring parity. No change to the search handler/manager/model is warranted.
faithfulness: Jellyfin's SearchManager fans a term across item names, people, genres, studios, and artists and unions the ranked hits; genres/studios/etc. are BaseItems, so a Genre named 'Action' is a searchable hint. Hermit already mirrors this: genres are materialized as BaseItems by-name rows (id = ItemValueId, Type='Genre') and the name-contains search returns them. The remaining behavioral gap is upstream metadata acquisition — Jellyfin runs TMDB/OMDb by default and thus has the 'Action' genre to search; Hermit must have that genre populated (via enabled remote providers or NFO) to match.
verify: Prove search itself is correct: seed a Genre by-name row and search for a substring — `cargo nextest run -p hermit-core search_manager` (existing hints_are_ranked_by_relevance shows the name-contains path returns materialized rows; adding a BaseItemKind::Genre 'Action' seed + searchTerm 'a' returns 1 hint). Prove the real gap: scan the same media into Hermit with `--features tmdb` (or with an NFO carrying <genre>Action</genre>) and re-run benchmark/parity.sh — search_hints then matches J=1 H=1. With remote providers off and no NFO, H=0 is expected.

root_cause: Each /UserViews view is a CollectionFolder row whose Path is `{program_data_path}/root/default/{LibraryName}` (built in app_paths.rs: root_folder_path = program_data_path.join("root"); default_user_views_path = root/default; and virtual_folder_manager.rs ensure_collection_folder sets path = default_user_views_path.join(name)). The DTO copies that path verbatim (dto_service.rs:909 `dto.path = item.path.clone()`), and the view's Id is derived from the same path (virtual_folder_manager.rs:114 collection_folder_id -> derive_item_id(CollectionFolder, folder_path)). In the containers, program_data_path is /config for Jellyfin and /data for Hermit, so every view Path differs only by that prefix (/config/root/default/X vs /data/root/default/X). The differential harness aligns items by Path; because the two library views' Paths differ by the data-dir prefix they fail to align and are reported as "+2 whole-item set membership" extras. Jellyfin computes the identical path (RootFolderPath/default/{name}); given the same data-dir the Paths (and, via GetNewItemId, the ids) would match. Only one CollectionFolder is emitted per library (no extra UserView/grouped views — those are explicitly deferred in user_view_manager.rs), so the view count itself matches; the divergence is purely the data-dir-prefixed Path used as the alignment key.
proposed_fix: none needed — the view Path (and its path-derived Id) differ only by the container data-dir prefix (/config vs /data). Both servers compute the same `{data_dir}/root/default/{LibraryName}` path; with a shared data-dir they would be byte-identical. The "+2" is a Path-keyed alignment artifact of the two synthetic libraries, not an extra-item bug. To silence it in the harness, normalize the data-dir prefix (or exclude Path) when aligning /UserViews items, exactly as ids/dates are already denylisted.
faithfulness: Jellyfin builds a CollectionFolder/UserView's physical path as `ApplicationPaths.RootFolderPath/default/{name}` (RootFolderPath = ProgramDataPath/root), and its Id from GetNewItemId over that path. Hermit matches this exactly; the sole difference is ProgramDataPath (/config in the Jellyfin container, /data in Hermit's). Emitting one CollectionFolder per configured library, name-sorted, with no synthetic grouped views also matches stock Jellyfin for an ungrouped setup.
verify: Run both servers with the SAME data-dir mount path (or normalize the leading data-dir when comparing) and re-diff GET /UserViews: the two views align by Path and the "+2" disappears. Locally: GET /UserViews on Hermit returns one item per configured library with Path `{data_dir}/root/default/{Name}` — confirm the only cross-server delta is the /config-vs-/data prefix.

root_cause: The write path is correct but the read path never consults it. `add_to_collection` (crates/hermit-core/src/collection_manager.rs:146-157) records membership only as a `LinkedChildren` row (manual link, ChildType=0) via `upsert_linked_child`; it never touches the child's `BaseItems.ParentId` column, and nothing writes an `AncestorIds` closure row for the link. When a client then browses `GET /Items?parentId=<collectionId>` non-recursively, the query translator (translate_query.rs:180-183) filters with `bi."ParentId" = <collectionId>` — a physical-parent equality — which no collection member satisfies, so 0 rows return. Even with `Recursive=true` the recursive branch (translate_query.rs:170-179) only walks the `AncestorIds` closure, which is likewise never populated for manual linked children. There is no BoxSet/Folder dispatch anywhere in the query path (items.rs:209-211 explicitly documents "the box-set/collection-type dispatch ... are deferred"; item_repository.rs get_items is uniform), so a BoxSet parentId is treated like any physical folder. Jellyfin instead loads the parent, sees it is a Folder/BoxSet, and returns its children from LinkedChildren — hence the add is visible there. Note this is the same LinkedChildren storage that get_playlist_items/get_collections_containing_item read correctly; only the generic /Items?parentId browse is blind to it.
proposed_fix: Make a BoxSet/Playlist parentId resolve through LinkedChildren the way Jellyfin's Folder.GetChildren does. Two viable shapes: (a) preferred — in the /Items handler (items.rs get_items) or in item_repository get_items, when parent_id resolves to a BoxSet/Playlist stored type, dispatch to the linked-children read (union the manual LinkedChildren.ChildId set into the result / the item_ids filter) instead of the plain ParentId equality; (b) alternatively, extend the non-recursive parent_id predicate in translate_query.rs:180-183 to also match rows whose Id is in LinkedChildren for that ParentId, e.g. `AND (bi."ParentId" = ?P OR bi."Id" IN (SELECT "ChildId" FROM "LinkedChildren" WHERE "ParentId" = ?P AND "ChildType" = 0))`, and for the recursive branch write AncestorIds rows for linked children on add. Option (a) is the faithful port (BoxSet is a Folder whose children ARE its LinkedChildren).
faithfulness: In Jellyfin, ItemsController.GetItems loads the parentId item; a BoxSet is a Folder, so it calls folder.GetItemList/GetChildren, and BoxSet's children are its LinkedChildren (manual links added by CollectionManager.AddToCollectionAsync). So a member added via POST /Collections/{id}/Items is returned by /Items?parentId={id}. Hermit must resolve a BoxSet/Playlist parent through LinkedChildren rather than the physical ParentId column.
collision_risk: library_manager.rs / translate_query.rs (parent_id predicate) and item_repository.rs get_items are hot; the items.rs handler dispatch is the lower-collision insertion point
verify: Unit: seed a Movie, create a BoxSet, add_to_collection, then call the item repository get_items with InternalItemsQuery{ parent_id = boxset_id, recursive = false } and assert the movie is returned (mirrors the existing create_collection_persists_row_and_members test but through the browse query rather than get_collections_containing_item). End-to-end: POST /Collections then POST /Collections/{id}/Items?ids=<movie>, then GET /Items?parentId=<id> and assert TotalRecordCount == 1.
